title: Call Centre Advisor
description:
DK Recruitment are seeking a Call Centre Advisor to join a busy customer service team in Plymouth. This is a great opportunity for someone with strong communication skills, a confident telephone manner and good IT skills who enjoys helping customers and working in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities:
- Handle incoming customer calls.
- Record customer requests accurately and ensure jobs are allocated promptly.
- Monitor and chase outstanding jobs to ensure agreed targets and timescales are met.
- Provide a high level of customer service, keeping customers informed throughout the process.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure data is entered correctly into company systems.
- Follow company procedures and quality standards.
- Identify and escalate issues where further support or approval is required.
- Work closely with colleagues to ensure the smooth running of daily operations.
- Complete general administrative duties as required.

The Ideal Candidate:
- Previous experience in a call centre or customer service role.
- Excellent communication and active listening skills.
- Confident using computers and customer management systems.
- Strong attention to detail and accurate data entry skills.
- Able to work well under pressure and manage multiple tasks.
- A proactive approach, with the ability to use initiative when required.
- A reliable team player with a positive attitude.

title: Resource Management Planner
description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Resource Management Planner to work within the Devon & Cornwall Police Force

Location: Plymouth
Contract Type: Temporary
Hourly Rate: 14.10 per hour
End Date: February 2027
Working Pattern: Full Time, Monday to Friday 37 hours per week

Please note this role is subject to POLICE VETTING you must have been residing within the UK for a minimum of 5 years

Are you passionate about resource management and planning? Our client is seeking a dedicated and skilled Resource Planner to join their team in Plymouth. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to operational policing by ensuring optimal staffing levels and responding effectively to the dynamic demands of the organisation.

Key Responsibilities:

As the Resource Planner, you will play a pivotal role in delivering effective resource plans to meet the diverse needs of various business areas. Your main responsibilities will include:
- Maintaining Staffing Levels: Ensure adequate staffing for daily policing activities and planned or spontaneous operations.
- Addressing Shortfalls: Proactively identify and report any staffing shortfalls, escalating issues as necessary.
- Data Management: Accurately record data within the Force IT Systems to enable the creation of comprehensive resource plans.
- First Point of Contact: Provide professional and courteous support for resource management inquiries, handling requests and issues with confidence.
- Skill Base Maintenance: Support the upkeep of the organisational skill base, ensuring staff have the appropriate training and skills.
- Reporting & Analysis: Produce insightful reports to aid managers in making informed resourcing decisions.

Essential Qualifications and Skills:

To thrive in this role, candidates should possess:
- A solid understanding of resource management and planning, along with knowledge of relevant IT systems.
- Familiarity with Working Time Regulations.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, enabling effective interaction with staff at all levels, including senior officers.
- Proficiency in MS Office, especially Excel, Teams, and Outlook.
- The ability to analyse large data sets and quickly identify gaps or inconsistencies.
- Proven experience of working under pressure and meeting tight deadlines.
- Strong negotiation and influencing skills.

Competency Framework:

The ideal candidate will embody the following competencies:
- Emotional awareness
- Ownership and accountability
- Collaboration and teamwork
- Support and inspiration
- Critical analysis
- Innovation and open-mindedness

Why Join Our Client?

This temporary position offers a unique chance to be part of an organisation that plays a vital role in public safety. The successful applicant will benefit from a supportive environment where they can develop their skills and contribute to meaningful outcomes.

If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to utilise your resource planning expertise, don't miss out!

How to Apply:

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by submitting their CV and a cover letter detailing their relevant experience. The selection process will focus on identifying individuals who align with the organisational values and can contribute positively to the team.

Become a key player in ensuring that the organisation meets its staffing needs effectively. Apply today and take the next step in your professional journey!

title: Scheduling Co-ordinator Part time
description:
Scheduling Coordinator - Part time

Location: Plymouth
Reports to: Branch Manager
Hours: Part-time, 2-3 days per week (up to 22 hours)
Salary: 26,400 per annum (pro rata)

About Universal Fire & Security

Universal Fire & Security is a trusted provider of fire and security solutions, delivering high-quality installation, maintenance, and support services to customers across the region. As part of the growing Ranger Group, we are proud to be part of a nationwide network of specialist businesses committed to raising industry standards and providing complete peace of mind for our clients.

We are looking for an organised and proactive Scheduling Coordinator to join our team in Plymouth. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys coordinating people, managing schedules, building customer relationships, and contributing to the success of a growing business.

The Role

As Scheduling Coordinator, you will play a key role in ensuring the efficient delivery of installation projects. You will be responsible for managing engineer schedules, coordinating resources, liaising with customers, and supporting the wider installation team to ensure projects are completed smoothly and on time.

This position is ideal for an adaptable individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is keen to develop their skills as the business continues to grow.

Key Responsibilities

Scheduling & Coordination
- Manage engineer diaries and schedule installation, pre-installation, and after-care visits.
- Coordinate site visits for engineers and sales personnel.
- Liaise with engineers to support efficient project delivery and workflow planning.
- Maintain project planners and track installation progress.
- Attend installation and planning meetings to support operational efficiency.
- Schedule installation handovers and snagging reviews.

Customer Service & Communication
- Build and maintain strong relationships with customers.
- Keep clients informed throughout the installation process.
- Conduct customer care calls following service visits.
- Handle incoming telephone enquiries and provide administrative support.

Administration & Systems
- Maintain accurate customer records using SIMPRO and FieldMotion.
- Input new customer information into company systems.
- Prepare job packs, installation paperwork, and welcome packs.
- Scan and upload documentation to internal systems.
- Produce quotations for parts and labour and support quotation preparation.
- Compile weekly and monthly operational reports and figures.
- Chase outstanding quotations when required.
- Prepare and collate monthly timesheets.

Resource & Compliance Support

Order equipment and materials for installation projects.

Monitor van stock levels and arrange replenishment where required.

Support training administration, including maintaining training records and assisting apprentice development.

Assist with health and safety administration, including engineer audits, vehicle checks, PPE monitoring, toolbox talks, and compliance documentation.

Support annual audits and wider business compliance activities.

What We're Looking For

Excellent organisational and planning skills.

Strong communication and customer service abilities.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a busy environment.

High attention to detail and accuracy.

Confident using Microsoft Office and business management systems.

Experience in scheduling, coordination, administration, or customer service is desirable.

Experience within the fire, security, construction, engineering, or service industries would be advantageous but is not essential.

Benefits

26,400 per annum (pro rata).

Pension scheme.

Private health insurance.

Life insurance.

Employee Assistance Programme.

25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata), with the option to purchase additional leave.

Clear opportunities for career progression within the Ranger Group.

Supportive and collaborative team environment.

Equal Opportunities

Universal Fire & Security and the Ranger Group are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation.

Apply today and become part of a growing team where your contribution truly makes a difference.

title: Receptionist
description: Receptionist Band 2 (20 hours per week) - Fixed Term - 12 Months The Glenbourne Unit are looking for a friendly and organised individual to join our team as a Receptionist at The Glenbourne Unit. This role is key to providing a welcoming and professional first point of contact for patients, visitors, and staff. Responsibilities include managing the reception desk, handling telephone enquiries, supporting administrative tasks, and ensuring smooth day-to-day operations. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication skills, a positive attitude, and the ability to work effectively in a busy healthcare environment. Provide front-of-house support for customers and visitors, acting as first point of enquiry and signposting to relevant services. Promote the departments image by ensuring notices and leaflets are current and well presented. Record and escalate complaints, compliments, and suggestions appropriately. title: Medical Receptionist
description: Church View Surgery is looking to recruit a friendly, professional and enthusiastic Medical Receptionist to join our busy and supportive practice team. As the first point of contact for patients and visitors, the successful candidate will play a vital role in delivering excellent customer service and ensuring patients receive the support they need. The role involves a combination of reception and administrative duties, including managing appointments, responding to patient enquiries, signposting patients to appropriate services, processing requests, and supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. We are seeking an individual with excellent communication and organisational skills who can remain calm under pressure, work effectively as part of a team and demonstrate a caring and compassionate approach to patient care. Previous experience in a reception, customer service or healthcare environment would be advantageous, although full training will be provided. Working at Church View Surgery offers the opportunity to be part of a forward-thinking, patient-centred practice serving approximately 12,600 patients. We are a partner-led practice rated Good by the CQC and are proud members of the Mewstone Primary Care Network, committed to delivering high-quality care and continuously improving services for our local community. The Medical Receptionist will provide a professional, friendly and efficient reception service, acting as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Key responsibilities include: Greeting patients and visitors and assisting with enquiries. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient requests in a courteous and professional manner. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments using SystmOne and SystmConnect. Processing online consultation requests and directing patients to the most appropriate service. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient records. Updating demographic information and ensuring patient details are current. Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence, emails and electronic communications. Scanning and attaching documents to patient records. Processing repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice procedures. Assisting patients with accessing online services and the NHS App. Monitoring and actioning tasks and workflow requests within agreed timescales. Maintaining confidentiality and complying with data protection and information governance requirements. Supporting clinicians and colleagues with administrative duties. Maintaining a clean, safe and welcoming reception environment. Working collaboratively with the wider practice team to deliver excellent customer service and high-quality patient care Hours - 22.25 per week - Tuesday 08.00-13.15, Wednesday 08.00-17.00 and Friday 09.30-18.30 Job Title: Medical Receptionist Responsible to: Reception Manager / Operations Manager Church View Surgery is seeking a friendly, professional and highly organised Medical Receptionist to join our busy practice team. The successful candidate will act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals, ensuring that all interactions are managed with courtesy, efficiency and compassion. The Medical Receptionist plays a vital role in the delivery of high-quality primary care services, providing a comprehensive reception and administrative service to support both patients and the wider clinical team. Working within a fast-paced environment, the post holder will be responsible for managing appointments, processing patient requests, maintaining accurate patient records and supporting the day-to-day operation of the practice. The role requires excellent communication skills, the ability to remain calm under pressure, a commitment to confidentiality and a patient-centred approach. Full training will be provided; however, experience in a customer service, administrative or healthcare environment would be advantageous. Welcome patients, visitors and healthcare professionals in a professional, friendly and courteous manner. Act as the first point of contact for all face-to-face, telephone and electronic enquiries. Ensure patients receive the highest standard of customer service at all times. Manage reception desk activities effectively and efficiently. Respond to patient enquiries and requests, escalating where appropriate. Deal with difficult situations professionally and sensitively whilst maintaining patient confidentiality. Ensure waiting areas remain tidy, safe and welcoming. Assist patients with accessing services and navigating the healthcare system. Process appointment requests in accordance with practice protocols. Book, amend and cancel appointments using SystmOne. Process and manage patient requests received through SystmConnect. Undertake care navigation and signposting to ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician or service. Maintain a thorough understanding of appointment templates and booking protocols. Support the management of clinician appointment availability. Liaise with clinical staff regarding urgent appointments and patient needs. Assist with appointment reminders, recalls and follow-up appointments where required. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle a high volume of calls whilst maintaining excellent customer service. Transfer calls and relay messages accurately. Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external organisations. Manage shared inboxes and electronic communications in a timely manner. Recognise when enquiries require escalation to clinical or management teams. Register new patients in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate, up-to-date patient demographic information. Process patient registrations, deductions and record transfers. Scan, upload and accurately file correspondence and clinical documentation into patient records. Monitor and action workflow tasks and administrative requests. Support the processing of repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies. Assist with the management of incoming and outgoing correspondence. Process test result requests in line with practice protocols. Support recall programmes and patient communication campaigns. Undertake data entry and maintain accurate electronic records. Assist with audits, reports and administrative projects as requested. Develop and maintain a thorough working knowledge of SystmOne. Use SystmConnect to manage and process online consultation requests. Ensure all patient interactions and actions are recorded accurately within the clinical system. Maintain the integrity and confidentiality of electronic patient records. Follow practice protocols when managing electronic workflows and patient communications. Work collaboratively with clinicians, administrative colleagues and the wider multidisciplinary team. Support colleagues during periods of annual leave, sickness or increased workload. Participate actively in team meetings and practice events. Contribute to a positive and supportive team environment. Share knowledge and best practice with colleagues. The post holder will have access to sensitive patient, staff and organisational information and must maintain strict confidentiality at all times. All duties must be carried out in accordance with Data Protection legislation, Information Governance requirements and Practice policies. The successful candidate will be expected to: Maintain patient confidentiality at all times. Ensure personal and sensitive information is managed appropriately. Follow all GDPR and Information Governance procedures. Report any breaches or concerns in accordance with practice policy. The post holder is responsible for promoting and maintaining a safe working environment for patients, visitors and colleagues. This includes: Following all health and safety policies and procedures. Maintaining clean and tidy work areas. Reporting hazards, accidents and incidents appropriately. Participating in mandatory health and safety training. Following infection prevention and control procedures. Maintaining a clear desk policy and secure handling of information. Supporting the security of the practice premises. Church View Surgery is committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion. The post holder will be expected to: Treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity and respect. Provide a welcoming and inclusive service to all individuals. Work in a manner that supports equality of opportunity. Respect differing backgrounds, beliefs and needs. The post holder will be expected to: Participate in annual appraisals and performance reviews. Complete all mandatory training requirements. Take responsibility for their own professional development. Actively participate in learning opportunities to develop skills and knowledge. Keep up to date with practice procedures and NHS guidance relevant to the role. This job description is intended as an outline of the main duties and responsibilities of the post. The post holder may be required to undertake other duties appropriate to the role, commensurate with the level of responsibility and as directed by the Reception Manager, Operations Manager or Practice Partners. The duties may be amended from time to time to meet the changing needs of the practice.
